name: Module 3: load, lysis, wash (translated from Szonja's file)
description: TRANSLATED by tools/convert_module3.py from chip/modules/module3_step1_3.json (Step 3, substeps 1–3: load, lysis, wash (main capsule trap); inputs: chip_geometry_requirements.xlsx (Sizing Calculator, Step 3 rows 1–3), 7 Nov 2026). Do not edit by hand: edit the source and re-run the converter. Ids, trap, gaps, channel size and capsule figures are the source's; layout, footprint, layers, channel routes and valve construction are inferred and marked placeholder. Open questions for the owner: (1) the design uses seven valves, and the MVP rule is no valves; (2) the 25 um retention gap and 140 um channels are far below what the laser cutter makes (Module 1's cut features are 0.8 mm), so how is it fabricated (bought mesh, embossing)? (3) footprint, material and port positions.

footprint.note: Inferred: the source gives the trap (28.3 mm square) but no board size.

layers.note: Material not in the source; must tolerate 4 M guanidinium thiocyanate.
Trap height 350 um from the source; the 150 um channels need a second, shallower depth.

chambers.note: square, wide and flat; holds 650,000 capsules in ~4 layers (packed volume 182.4 uL, fill 0.65). Retention 25 um (pillar row or mesh at the outlet side; allowed 21–28 um) on the outlet (right) side: keeps 70 µm capsules, passes buffer, lysate and debris. inlet and outlet manifolds across the full width so buffer sweeps the whole bed. must tolerate 4 M guanidinium thiocyanate. Size, height, volume and gap from the source; position inferred; retention type: the source says 'pillar row or mesh', pillars assumed here.
